verdict.rationale: WorkOS documents AuthKit as a spec-compatible OAuth authorization server that can manage access to your own MCP server (workos-docs-27, workos-docs-8), with built-in support for MCP and OAuth applications (workos-docs-31). This is distinct from WorkOS's own management MCP server, which is not credited here. Token scoping and verification are only implied by the 'spec-compatible' claim and by session JWTs carrying roles in the general RBAC docs (workos-supp-rbac-jwt). missing for 10: explicit documentation of per-scope tokens and token verification (e.g., JWKS validation) for MCP clients, details on client registration for remote agents, independent or hands-on corroboration of the MCP auth flow
